newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas still pressured late by profit taking.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas still pressured late by profit taking.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures remained on the defensive late Tuesday despite reports of steady to firmer physical prices, still undermined by profit taking after recent sharp gains, market sources said.
At 1435 EDT, September tumbled 8.6 cents to $2.50 per million British thermal units, while October was 7.8 cents lower at $2.50. Other deferreds were down by 0.1 to six cents.

"There's a fair amount of length out there. They may be expecting to see a larger (AGA stock) build this week because of the cooler weather and decided to take the money and run," said one Houston-based trader, noting chart watchers also may have seen a sell signal after September's failure today to probe new highs.
Early injection estimates for Wednesday's weekly AGA inventory report range from 60 to 90 bcf versus an 80 bcf build for the same week last year.

While lagging stock builds in recent weeks fueled more bullish sentiment, some expected a profit taking pullback after the 22 percent rally since late July, particularly with no weather support on the horizon and open interest now at record levels.
Cooler-than-normal weather is expected to cover most of the East and Midwest this week, while heat continues to bake much of the Southwest, according to Weather Services Corp.

Technical traders raised the possibility of a double top today, as September's climb on ACCESS to $2.604 just failed to breach its new contract high of $2.605 set yesterday. They pegged resistance first at the new high of $2.605, with further selling likely at the $2.64-2.655 spot continuation chart gap from late January. Support was seen at $2.47, $2.34 and $2.30, with better buying likely at $2.25-2.27.
In the cash Tuesday, Gulf Coast prices were up slightly to $2.50 or better. Midcon pipes were unhanged in the mid-$2.40s. New York city gate gas also was up slightly to the mid-$2.70s.
NYMEX said 41,766 contracts traded at 1400 EDT. Hub open interest on Aug 11 rose 2,745 contracts to a record 217,654.

On the KCBT, September skidded 7.5 cents to $2.405, while deferreds were steady to eight cents lower. The East/West spread narrowed by 1.1 cents to 9.5 cents (NYMEX premium). ((--J Silha, New York Power Desk 212-859-1624))
